values: Scope, matching rules, limitations and reproducible evidence for this workbook.
K-Electric organization, source system KE_LOGISTICS. Queries ran in a repeatable-read, read-only transaction.
Prevents the audit from changing production and keeps all extracted tables at one point in time.
Live tables: global_products, legacy_product_mappings, organization_inventory, legacy_import_batches, order_items
Reconstructs what the portal already held when the first migration began; includes Sugar even though it was later mapped.
A mapped product created by the initial ID range 165–308, tagged legacySource=KE_LOGISTICS, or carrying a KE-/KE-history code. Product 7 is classified as reused, not imported.
Separates newly created legacy rows from the pre-existing product that the importer correctly reused.
Live mappings and product lineage fields

Compared every imported row with every pre-import row, and every imported row with every other imported row. Used normalized words, common spelling variants, token overlap and edit similarity; then manually reviewed brand, variant, size, pack and price evidence.
Fuzzy score is a screening aid, not the decision itself.
Same product identity and pack are supported by the names and units.
Suitable for merge planning after dependency checks.
Strong identity match, but one meaningful detail is omitted or unclear.
Plausible relationship with a material size, brand, flavour, variant or pack-basis ambiguity.
Do not merge without supplier, invoice or catalogue evidence.
Prices are shown in PKR and price variance is calculated as (imported − comparison) / comparison.
Price supports review but cannot prove identity because price tiers and case/unit basis can differ.
Counts are current K-Electric order_items rows referencing each product.
High counts indicate dependency and historical-reporting risk during a merge.
The local pre-migration JSON backup was not used as authoritative evidence because its current SHA-256 does not match its sidecar.
Avoids basing conclusions on a file whose integrity check fails. The live ledger and timestamps provide the baseline instead.
Explains why punctuation spacing is handled but unit spacing and semantic aliases are not.
Explains the exact-match gate used during historical order migration.
Explains why an unmapped near-name product can be created.
Reads current mappings and inserts new global product, organization inventory and mapping rows.
